title: Transformation plan, maturity, psychological safety and sustainability
blurb: Apply the agile transformation plan, agile maturity, psychological safety and agile sustainability to a scenario's people and stage.
question: Easterholm is piloting agile on one project, and its social workers have little time and many doubts. Does it need an agile transformation plan, and how should it raise agile maturity?

teach.h: Four key concepts of agile transformation
teach.body: Formally: the Practitioner syllabus asks you to apply four key concepts of agile transformation: the agile transformation plan (2.7.1), agile maturity (2.7.3), psychological safety (2.7.4) and agile sustainability (2.7.5). The key metrics for agility are psychological safety, agile maturity and agile sustainability. In plain English: plan the change at the right scale, help people learn by doing, make it safe to speak up, and keep checking that agility is taking root.

teach.h: Agile maturity: the concepts the exam uses
teach.body: Growth mindset: anyone can learn, adapt and grow; often seen as the core of the agile mindset. Training and coaching: people need theory AND practical coaching on the job; informing them and leaving them to fend for themselves breeds frustration, a leading cause of demotivation and resistance; plan training and coaching to match the stages of the change. Servant leadership: lead by serving the team's needs. Rich communication: words plus emotion, body language and visuals.

teach.body: Psychological safety is essential for a productive, innovative agile environment: people feel safe to speak up, take risks and challenge ideas without fear of judgement or negative consequences. Two types appear in exam rationales. Inclusion safety: I feel accepted and can be myself. Contributor safety: I am encouraged to share my ideas and skills, and my contributions are respected.

teach.caption: First assessed in starting up or initiating a project through agile maturity assessments (12.4.1); trends can appear on the project dashboard.

teach.body: Easterholm County Council has very little agile experience and Care Online is its first PRINCE2 Agile project, so project manager Simon Archer updates the change management approach rather than writing a council-wide plan. Agile coach Gita Bhatt sets a training and coaching plan for the ten social-work champions, coaching them in real sprint reviews. She makes it safe for social workers to voice doubts about self-assessment, and a baseline maturity assessment in initiation tracks the three key metrics.

teach.text: Classic traps: an agile transformation plan produced by a project is an output (scope), not a benefit. A single pilot may need only an updated change management approach. Agile sustainability is a key metric of agility, not the sustainability performance target (the project's impact on the wider environment). Varying agile maturity is handled openly, not escalated.

items: Transformation plan: strategic goals plus short-term objectives, usually across several initiatives; can replace the change management approach.
Maturity: growth mindset, training AND on-the-job coaching, servant leadership, rich communication.
Psychological safety: speak up and challenge without fear; inclusion and contributor safety.
Key metrics: psychological safety, agile maturity, agile sustainability (maturity assessments).

summary: You can now decide whether a scenario needs an agile transformation plan or an updated change management approach, and choose actions that raise agile maturity and psychological safety. You can also name the three key metrics for agility and keep agile sustainability apart from the sustainability performance target.

A.q: Easterholm County Council is using Care Online as a pilot of agile ways of working; no other council project will change its approach this year. In the project initiation workshop, the project manager asks whether a full agile transformation plan is needed. What is MOST appropriate?
options: Write a transformation plan for every council department before Release 1
Update the project's change management approach to cover the pilot
Record the agile changes in the risk register as threats to the pilot
Leave agile adoption out of the PID until the pilot project has closed
A.why: A transformation plan typically spans several projects for enterprise-wide adoption; for a single pilot it may not be needed yet, and the change management approach can be updated instead (2.7.1).

whyNot.0: A council-wide plan suits enterprise adoption across initiatives, not one pilot project.
whyNot.2: The register records risks; it does not describe how the change will be managed.
whyNot.3: How the project manages the change belongs in the PID's change management approach now.

A.q: Easterholm will train ten social workers as product champions for Care Online. Project manager Simon Archer proposes emailing them the new user-story guide and letting them work it out during sprint reviews. Which action BEST supports agile maturity?
options: Send a longer guide with a glossary so champions can study at home
Limit coaching to the digital team, as social workers are the users
Combine training with on-the-job coaching set out in a coaching plan
Introduce a backlog tool first so the champions see how stories work
A.why: People need theoretical training and practical coaching on the job; PRINCE2 Agile suggests a training and coaching plan mapped to the stages of the change (2.7.3).

whyNot.0: More reading is still informing people and leaving them to fend for themselves.
whyNot.1: As many people as possible should understand what is changing and why, not just the developers.
whyNot.3: Introducing tools before people understand the change is premature.

A.q: In Care Online sprint reviews, social workers stay silent about their worry that self-assessment will misjudge people's needs, because they fear being seen as resisting the change. Which concept should the agile coach focus on FIRST?
options: Psychological safety, so people can challenge ideas without fear
Servant leadership, so the coach meets every social worker's needs
Rich communication, so that reviews use more visuals and diagrams
A transformation plan, so that council-wide goals are made clear
A.why: Psychological safety means people feel safe to express themselves, take risks and challenge ideas without fear of judgement or negative consequences (2.7.4).

whyNot.1: Servant leadership is a leadership style; the problem is fear of speaking up.
whyNot.2: Better visuals do not remove the fear that keeps people silent.
whyNot.3: Council-wide goals do not address why people will not voice concerns.

B.q: Easterholm's draft project canvas lists 'an agile transformation plan for adult social care' under expected benefits, with a target date in month 12. What correction is MOST appropriate?
options: Move it to major risks, because agile adoption may fail
Keep it under benefits, measured by the number of staff trained
Move it to costs, because the agile coach's contract funds it
Move it to scope, because a plan is an output, not a benefit
B.why: A benefit is a measurable improvement from an outcome; a transformation plan is an output, part of the project product, so it belongs under scope (Glossary, 6.3.2.1).

whyNot.0: Adoption risks can be listed, but the plan itself is a deliverable.
whyNot.1: Counting trained staff measures an activity; the plan is still an output.
whyNot.2: The coach's fees are a cost, but the plan is a product the project delivers.

B.q: Oliver Grant, Easterholm's delivery manager, spends his time removing obstacles for the digital team, getting people the access and equipment they need and checking they are coping, rather than directing their work. Which agile maturity concept does this BEST show?
options: Growth mindset
Servant leadership
Training and coaching
Rich communication
B.why: Servant leadership (Robert Greenleaf) means leading by serving: putting team members' needs first and making sure they are supported and have what they need (2.7.3).

whyNot.0: Growth mindset is the belief that anyone can learn and grow.
whyNot.2: Training and coaching is about theory plus on-the-job practice.
whyNot.3: Rich communication is about words plus emotion, body language and visuals.

B.q: During Care Online's initiation, agile coach Gita Bhatt proposes an agile maturity assessment to set a baseline for the key metrics of agility, to be tracked through each stage. Which metrics should the assessment cover?
options: Velocity, story points and burn-down progress for each team
Time, cost and scope tolerances for each stage of the project
Psychological safety, agile maturity and agile sustainability
Benefits, sustainability and risk performance targets for the project
B.why: The key metrics for agility are psychological safety, agile maturity and agile sustainability, first assessed in starting up or initiating through agile maturity assessments (2.7.6, 12.4.1).

whyNot.0: These measure delivery progress, not agility.
whyNot.1: Tolerances are set for project performance, not as metrics of agility.
whyNot.3: These are performance targets of the project, not the key metrics for agility.

C.q: After sprint 1, assistant director Joan Whitaker proposes removing from the champion group the social workers who struggled with the new ways of working, saying 'some people just aren't agile'. Is this an appropriate response, and why?
options: Yes, because the champions must model agile behaviour for others
Yes, because varying agile maturity should be escalated to the board
No, because a growth mindset holds that anyone can learn and adapt
No, because rich communication needs every champion to stay involved
C.why: A growth mindset is the belief that any person can learn, adapt and grow, and is often seen as the core of the agile mindset (2.7.3); early struggle calls for coaching, not exclusion.

whyNot.0: Champions do model behaviour, but that does not justify writing people off after one sprint.
whyNot.1: Varying maturity is handled transparently as lessons are learned, not escalated (Table 5.1).
whyNot.3: Rich communication is about how information is conveyed, not who stays in a group.

C.q: Because social workers have little time, Simon Archer proposes replacing their attendance at sprint reviews with a written summary of each increment, emailed every fortnight. Is this an appropriate way to involve them, and why?
options: Yes, because it respects the social workers' very high caseloads
Yes, because written records support the project's audit trail
No, because the project board must attend every sprint review
No, because rich communication conveys far more than written words
C.why: Rich communication means conveying words plus emotions, body language and visuals; in short iterations there is no time for misunderstandings (2.7.3).

whyNot.0: Caseloads matter, but a text-only summary loses the richness agile depends on.
whyNot.1: Records have value, but they do not replace rich two-way communication.
whyNot.2: The board does not attend every review; this is not the reason.

C.q: Near the end of Care Online, the agile coach's contract is ending. The project manager arranges a final agile maturity assessment covering psychological safety, agile maturity and agile sustainability, and compares it with the baseline from initiation. Is this an appropriate application, and why?
options: Yes, because agile sustainability is a key metric of agility to assess
Yes, because the sustainability performance target covers ways of working
No, because maturity assessments are held in starting up and not later
No, because the climate pledge is the measure of sustainability here
C.why: Psychological safety, agile maturity and agile sustainability are the key metrics for agility, assessed through agile maturity assessments from starting up or initiation onwards (2.7.6, 12.4.1).

whyNot.1: The sustainability performance target is about the project's impact on the wider environment.
whyNot.2: They are first assessed early, then tracked; trends can appear on the project dashboard.
whyNot.3: The climate pledge relates to the sustainability performance target, not agile sustainability.

reteach.title: Scale, learning, safety, staying power
reteach.question: Can you apply the four transformation factors to a scenario?

blocks.body: Scale: is this one pilot (update the change management approach) or many initiatives (agile transformation plan)? Learning: do people get training AND coaching on the job? Safety: can people speak up without fear? Staying power: are psychological safety, agile maturity and agile sustainability being assessed and tracked?

blocks.text: A transformation plan is an output, not a benefit. Agile sustainability is not the sustainability performance target.

explain.body: A plan guiding an initiative to adopt (more) agility: high-level goals aligning target states to strategy, plus short-term objectives for practical implementation. It usually spans several projects; in the project initiation workshop it can replace the change management approach if needed.

test.q: Easterholm's cabinet decides Care Online will be the first of several projects moving all council services to agile ways of working over three years. In the project initiation workshop, what should be agreed about the change management approach?
options: Keep it unchanged, as cabinet decisions sit outside the project
Replace it with an agile transformation plan for the wider change
Move the agile goals into the benefits management approach
Hand the agile goals to the delivery team's product backlog
test.why: For enterprise-wide adoption across several initiatives, an agile transformation plan fits, and in the project initiation workshop it can replace the change management approach (2.7.1, Table 13.7).

whyNot.0: The wider change affects how this project manages change, so the approach must reflect it.
whyNot.2: Agile adoption goals are not benefits to be realized from this project's products.
whyNot.3: A team's product backlog holds user stories, not the council's transformation goals.

explain.body: Inform people, then help them apply the change through theoretical training AND practical coaching on the job. Leaving people to fend for themselves breeds frustration, demotivation and resistance. As many people as possible should understand what is changing and why.

test.q: Easterholm's front door team, managed by Paul Henshaw, will start handling online self-assessments in Release 2. Which approach BEST prepares the team?
options: A training and coaching plan with practice on real cases
A one-off presentation on agile theory from the agile coach
An email explaining the new process the week before go-live
A self-study course for the team leader to cascade later
test.why: People need theoretical training and practical coaching on the job, ideally in a training and coaching plan mapped to the stages of the change (2.7.3).

whyNot.1: Theory alone lacks the practical application needed.
whyNot.2: Informing people and leaving them to fend for themselves undermines the change.
whyNot.3: Relying on one person to cascade misses on-the-job coaching for the whole team.

explain.body: Inclusion safety: people feel accepted and valued and can be themselves. Contributor safety: people are encouraged to share ideas and skills, and their contributions are respected.

test.q: An occupational therapist joining Care Online sprints feels welcome in the team, but her suggestions about accessible design are rarely taken up and she has stopped offering them. Which type of psychological safety is MOST lacking?
options: Inclusion safety
Growth mindset
Servant leadership
Contributor safety
test.why: Contributor safety means being encouraged to share ideas and skills openly, knowing contributions are appreciated and respected (2.7.4).

whyNot.0: She feels welcome and accepted, so inclusion safety is present.
whyNot.1: Growth mindset is an agile maturity concept, not a type of psychological safety.
whyNot.2: Servant leadership is a leadership style, not a type of psychological safety.

explain.body: Agile sustainability is one of the three key metrics for agility, assessed in agile maturity assessments. The sustainability performance target is about how the project affects the wider environment, such as Easterholm's aim to cut paper and travel.

test.q: Easterholm wants Care Online to cut paper forms and staff travel to people's homes, supporting its climate pledge. Which concept is this?
options: Agile sustainability, a key metric for agility
Agile maturity, tracked in maturity assessments
The sustainability performance target
Psychological safety, a key metric for agility
test.why: Sustainability as a performance target describes how the project will impact the wider environment (1.3.2).

whyNot.0: Agile sustainability concerns how well agility lasts, not environmental impact.
whyNot.1: Agile maturity concerns how mature people's agile working is.
whyNot.3: Psychological safety concerns people feeling safe to speak up.
